name: iam:PassRole + batch:CreateComputeEnvironment + batch:CreateJobQueue + batch:RegisterJobDefinition + batch:SubmitJob
description: A principal with iam:PassRole and broad Batch permissions can escalate privileges by creating the entire AWS Batch pipeline from scratch — a Fargate compute environment, a job queue, and a job definition that passes an admin IAM role as the jobRoleArn — then submitting a job whose container runs with the admin role's credentials. Unlike batch-001, no pre-existing Batch infrastructure is required. batch:CreateComputeEnvironment auto-creates an ECS cluster via the Batch service-linked role, so the attacker gets ECS task execution capability without any ECS permissions.
author: Seth Art

required.description: Must be able to pass the target admin IAM role and a Batch execution role to the Batch service
Creates a managed Fargate compute environment (auto-creates an ECS cluster via the Batch service-linked role)
Creates a job queue wired to the attacker-created compute environment
Registers a job definition with the admin role as jobRoleArn
Submits the job to the attacker-created queue

additional.description: Polls compute environment status during creation (CREATING -> VALID)
Verifies job queue creation and state
Polls job execution status to confirm completion
Discovers IAM roles to identify passable admin and execution roles
Discovers available VPC subnets for the Fargate compute environment
Discovers available security groups for the Fargate compute environment

admin: A role must exist that trusts ecs-tasks.amazonaws.com and has administrative permissions (e.g., AdministratorAccess)
An ECS task execution role must exist that trusts ecs-tasks.amazonaws.com with AmazonECSTaskExecutionRolePolicy
A VPC subnet with internet access (public subnet or NAT gateway) for Fargate tasks
A security group allowing outbound traffic for container image pulls and API calls
lateral: A role must exist that trusts ecs-tasks.amazonaws.com and has elevated permissions
An ECS task execution role must exist
A VPC subnet with internet access and an appropriate security group

references.title: Messing Around With AWS Batch For Privilege Escalations - Doyensec
How AWS Batch works with IAM
Actions defined by AWS Batch - Service Authorization Reference

options.name: ADMIN_ROLE_ARN
options.description: ARN of the IAM role to pass as jobRoleArn — the container will run with this role's credentials

options.name: EXECUTION_ROLE_ARN
options.description: ARN of the Fargate execution role (must trust ecs-tasks.amazonaws.com and have AmazonECSTaskExecutionRolePolicy)

options.name: SUBNET_ID
options.description: VPC subnet ID for the Fargate compute environment (must have internet access for image pulls and API calls)

options.name: SECURITY_GROUP_ID
options.description: Security group ID for the Fargate compute environment (must allow outbound traffic)

options.name: PAYLOAD
options.description: Payload type to execute inside the Batch job container. aws-cli runtime: backdoor/attach-policy, backdoor/create-access-key. generic runtime: backdoor/create-user, backdoor/create-role, backdoor/update-role-trust, exfil/https

options.name: CONTAINER_RUNTIME
options.description: Container entrypoint type: 'aws-cli' (default, registers amazon/aws-cli:latest) or 'generic' (registers IMAGE with sh + aws CLI — e.g. Ubuntu, Debian). exfil/https requires 'generic'.

options.name: IMAGE
options.description: Container image to use in the registered job definition. Defaults to 'amazon/aws-cli:latest' for aws-cli runtime, or 'ubuntu:latest' for generic runtime. The image must be accessible from the Fargate compute environment.

options.name: TARGET_PRINCIPAL
options.description: IAM username or role name to attach AdministratorAccess to (auto-resolved from caller identity if not set)

options.name: COMPUTE_ENV_NAME
options.description: Name for the new Batch compute environment to create

options.name: JOB_QUEUE_NAME
options.description: Name for the new Batch job queue to create

options.name: JOB_DEF_NAME
options.description: Name for the new Batch job definition to register

options.name: REGION
options.description: AWS region for Batch and IAM operations

options.name: CLEANUP
options.description: Deregister the job definition and detach AdministratorAccess from TARGET_PRINCIPAL after execution. Requires batch:DeregisterJobDefinition and iam:DetachUserPolicy/iam:DetachRolePolicy. Defaults to false because the lab's starting principal does not have these permissions; use 'workspace cleanup' with an elevated identity instead.

payloads.name: backdoor/attach-policy
payloads.description: Attach AdministratorAccess (or any managed policy) to an IAM user or role via Batch job container command

payloads.name: backdoor/create-access-key
payloads.description: Create programmatic access keys for an IAM user via Batch job container command

payloads.name: backdoor/create-role
payloads.description: Create an IAM role with AdministratorAccess and a custom trust policy via Batch job (requires CONTAINER_RUNTIME=generic)

payloads.name: backdoor/create-user
payloads.description: Create an IAM user with AdministratorAccess and optional console/programmatic access via Batch job (requires CONTAINER_RUNTIME=generic)

payloads.name: backdoor/update-role-trust
payloads.description: Append a trust policy statement to an existing IAM role via Batch job (requires CONTAINER_RUNTIME=generic with jq)

payloads.name: exfil/https
payloads.description: Exfiltrate Batch task role credentials to an attacker HTTPS endpoint; detects curl/wget/python at runtime (requires CONTAINER_RUNTIME=generic)
